title.zh: 卷372 列傳一百五十九 裕谦 谢朝恩 重祥 关天培 陈连升 祥福 江继芸 陈化成 海龄 葛雲飞 王锡朋 郑国鸿 朱贵
title.en: Volume 372 Biographies 159: Yu Qian, Xie Chaoen, Zhong Xiang, Guan Tianpei, Chen Liansheng, Xiang Fu, Jiang Jiyun, Chen Huacheng, Hai Ling, Ge Yunfei, Wang Xipeng, Zheng Guohong, Zhu Gui
title.raw: 卷372 列傳一百五十九 裕谦 谢朝恩 重祥 关天培 陈连升 祥福 江继芸 陈化成 海龄 葛雲飞 王锡朋 郑国鸿 朱贵

sentences.zh: =裕謙=裕謙，原名裕泰，字魯山，博羅忒氏，蒙古鑲黃旗人，一等誠勇公班第曾孫，綏遠城將軍巴祿孫。

translations.literal: Yu Qian, original name Yu Tai, style name Lushan, of the Boluote clan, a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner, great-grandson of Bandi, Duke of Cheng Courage of the first rank, and grandson of Balu, General of Suoyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, originally named Yu Tai and styled Lushan, was a Mongol of the Boluote clan in the Bordered Yellow Banner, the great-grandson of Bandi, a first-rank Duke of Cheng Courage, and the grandson of Balu, General of Suoyuan City.

sentences.zh: 父慶麟，京口副都統。

translations.literal: His father Qinglin was Deputy Commander-in-Chief at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinglin served as Deputy Commander-in-Chief at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 裕謙，嘉慶二十二年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Yu Qian passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-second year of the Jiaqing reign and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing, Yu Qian passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館改禮部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was assigned as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, then promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin training, he was made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，出為湖北荊州知府，始改今名。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, he was sent out as prefect of Jingzhou in Hubei and at this time changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang he took up the post of prefect of Jingzhou in Hubei, adopting his present name at that time.

sentences.zh: 調武昌，歷荊宜施道、江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Wuchang, then served successively as intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi Circuit and provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wuchang and subsequently served as intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi Circuit and as Jiangsu provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十九年，就遷布政使，署巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted in place to provincial treasurer, acted as governor, and soon received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted on site to provincial treasurer, served as acting governor, and shortly afterward received the permanent appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英兵陷定海，伊里布奉命往剿，裕謙代署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when British troops captured Dinghai, Yilibu was ordered to proceed to suppress them, and Yu Qian took over as acting governor-general of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, after British forces seized Dinghai, Yilibu was dispatched to lead the suppression campaign, and Yu Qian served as acting governor-general of Liangjiang in his stead.

sentences.zh: 時英艦遊奕海門外洋，江南戒嚴。

translations.literal: At the time British warships patrolled the outer waters off Haimen, and Jiangnan was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: British warships were then prowling the seas off Haimen, and Jiangnan was placed on high military alert.

sentences.zh: 裕謙赴寶山、上海籌防，檄徐州鎮總兵王志元，佐提督陳化成防海口。

translations.literal: Yu Qian went to Baoshan and Shanghai to organize defenses, and dispatched an order to Wang Zhiyuan, commanding general of Xuzhou, to assist Admiral Chen Huacheng in defending the harbor mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian went to Baoshan and Shanghai to organize the defense, ordering Wang Zhiyuan, commanding general of Xuzhou, to assist Admiral Chen Huacheng in guarding the harbor entrance.

sentences.zh: 疏陳規复定海之策，可無慮者四，難緩待者六，謂各省皆可言守，浙江必應議戰，且應速戰。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth a plan to recover Dinghai, citing four points that need not be worried over and six that could not be deferred, stating that while every province might speak of holding fast, Zhejiang must debate war and ought to do so swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he laid out a plan to retake Dinghai, identifying four reasons for confidence and six urgent concerns; he argued that while other provinces might talk only of holding their ground, Zhejiang had to commit to fighting—and to fighting at once.

sentences.zh: 又疏劾琦善五罪，略曰：「英人至天津，僅五船耳，琦善大張其事，遽稱：『畿疆、遼、瀋處處可虞，後來之艦尚多，勢將遍擾南北』。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial impeaching Qishan on five counts, stating in summary: "When the English reached Tianjin, there were only five ships, yet Qishan greatly exaggerated the affair and at once declared: 'The capital region, Liaodong, and Shenyang are everywhere at risk; more warships are still coming and will likely spread disturbance north and south.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial impeaching Qishan on five counts, writing in summary: "When the British reached Tianjin there were only five ships, yet Qishan grossly inflated the threat and immediately declared that the capital region, Liaodong, and Shenyang were all in danger, that more warships were still coming, and that the enemy would soon spread havoc across north and south.

sentences.zh: 冀聳聽聞，以掩其武備廢弛之咎。

translations.literal: He hoped to startle the court with alarm, so as to cover his own fault for the neglect of military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to alarm the court and thereby conceal his own failure to maintain the defenses.

sentences.zh: 張皇欺飾，其罪一。

translations.literal: Alarmist exaggeration and deceitful concealment—this is his first crime.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmist exaggeration and deliberate deception—this was his first offense.

sentences.zh: 英酋回粵以來，驕桀日甚，琦善惟責兵將謝過，別未設籌，將士解體，軍心沮喪。

translations.literal: Since the English leader returned to Guangdong, his arrogance has grown daily, yet Qishan only required officers and soldiers to apologize and made no other plans; the troops lost cohesion and army morale sank.
translations.idiomatic: Since the British commander returned to Guangdong, his arrogance had grown by the day, yet Qishan did nothing but demand apologies from his officers and men and made no other preparations; the army lost cohesion and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 彼軍乘敝，遂衄我師。

translations.literal: The enemy army took advantage of our weakness and thus routed our forces.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy seized on our weakness and routed our army.

sentences.zh: 我船砲縱不如彼，兵數何啻十倍。

translations.literal: Even if our ships and cannon are indeed inferior to theirs, our troop numbers are no less than ten times theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Even if our ships and guns were inferior, our numbers were at least ten times theirs.

sentences.zh: 琦善不防後路，事敗委過前人。

translations.literal: Qishan did not guard the rear, and when matters failed he shifted blame onto his predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan failed to secure the rear, and when defeat came he blamed those who had gone before him.

sentences.zh: 試思琦善未至粵時，未聞失機，其又何說？

translations.literal: Consider: before Qishan arrived in Guangdong, no loss of opportunity was heard of—what then can he say?
translations.idiomatic: Before Qishan ever reached Guangdong, no such missed opportunities were reported—what excuse could he offer?

sentences.zh: 弛備損威，其罪二。

translations.literal: Neglect of defense and damage to imperial prestige—this is his second crime.
translations.idiomatic: Neglect of the defenses and damage to imperial prestige—this was his second offense.

sentences.zh: 沙角、大角砲台既失，自應迅駐虎門，乃其奏中不及剿堵事，惟以覆書​​緩兵為詞，且囑浙省勿進兵。

translations.literal: Once the Shajiao and Dajiao batteries were lost, he should at once have stationed himself at Humen, yet in his memorials he said nothing of pursuing and blocking the enemy, using only reply letters as a pretext to delay action, and moreover instructed Zhejiang not to advance troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shajiao and Dajiao forts were lost, he should have moved swiftly to Humen, yet his memorials said nothing about pursuing or blocking the enemy; he used nothing but reply letters as a delaying tactic and even instructed Zhejiang not to advance its troops.

sentences.zh: 旋以給香港、即日通商定議，不俟交還定海後奏允奉行。

translations.literal: He then agreed to cede Hong Kong and open trade on the same day, without waiting for imperial approval after the return of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He then agreed to cede Hong Kong and open trade immediately, without waiting for imperial approval after Dinghai had been returned.

sentences.zh: 違例擅權，其罪三。

translations.literal: Violation of precedent and usurpation of authority—this is his third crime.
translations.idiomatic: Violation of precedent and abuse of authority—this was his third offense.

sentences.zh: 既畀香港換出定海，而英人仍欲通商寧波，銷售鴉片。

translations.literal: Having ceded Hong Kong in exchange for the recovery of Dinghai, the English still wish to trade at Ningbo and sell opium.
translations.idiomatic: Even after ceding Hong Kong in exchange for Dinghai, the British still wanted to trade at Ningbo and sell opium there.

sentences.zh: 何以不在粵翦斷葛藤？

translations.literal: Why did he not cut off these entanglements in Guangdong?
translations.idiomatic: Why did he not settle these entanglements once and for all in Guangdong?

sentences.zh: 將就苟且，其罪四。

translations.literal: Seeking only a makeshift settlement—this is his fourth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Settling for a makeshift compromise—this was his fourth offense.

sentences.zh: 義律僅外商首領，向來呈牘，自稱遠商遠職。

translations.literal: Elliot was merely the head of foreign merchants; in his past memorials he called himself a distant merchant holding a distant office.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot was only the head of the foreign merchants; in his past communications he had styled himself a distant trader holding a distant office.

sentences.zh: 上年在天津、浙江僭稱公使大臣，琦善不之詳，假以稱號。

translations.literal: Last year at Tianjin and in Zhejiang he presumptuously styled himself minister plenipotentiary, and Qishan did not investigate but lent him the title.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, at Tianjin and in Zhejiang, he had presumptuously styled himself minister plenipotentiary, and Qishan never looked into it but simply accepted the title.

sentences.zh: 失體招釁，其罪五。

translations.literal: Loss of dignity and invitation of provocation—this is his fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: Loss of dignity and invitation of provocation—this was his fifth offense.

sentences.zh: 琦善已為英人藐玩，各國輕視，不宜久於其任。」

translations.literal: Qishan has already been treated with contempt by the English and held in low regard by all nations; he should not remain long in his post."
translations.idiomatic: Qishan had already been treated with contempt by the British and held in low regard by other nations; he should not be kept in office much longer."

sentences.zh: 疏上，宣宗憤琦善受紿，斥伊里布附和，信裕謙忠直可恃。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, the Xuanzong Emperor was angered that Qishan had been deceived, rebuked Yilibu for echoing him, and trusted Yu Qian as loyal and upright and worthy of reliance.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Emperor Xuanzong was enraged that Qishan had been duped, rebuked Yilibu for going along with him, and declared Yu Qian loyal, upright, and trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，罷伊里布，以裕謙代之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year, Yilibu was dismissed and Yu Qian was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-first year, Yilibu was dismissed and Yu Qian was appointed to replace him.

sentences.zh: 裕謙至鎮海，英艦已去定海，渡海往治善後事宜。

translations.literal: When Yu Qian reached Zhenhai, the British warships had already left Dinghai; he crossed the sea to attend to post-disaster affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Qian reached Zhenhai, the British fleet had already left Dinghai, and he crossed the sea to handle the aftermath.

sentences.zh: 尋實授兩江總督，以浙事付巡撫劉韻珂、提督餘步雲，自回江南部署防務。

translations.literal: Soon he received formal appointment as governor-general of Liangjiang, entrusted Zhejiang affairs to Governor Liu Yunke and Admiral Yu Buyun, and returned himself to Jiangnan to deploy defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed governor-general of Liangjiang, left Zhejiang affairs to Governor Liu Yunke and Admiral Yu Buyun, and returned to Jiangnan to organize the defenses.

sentences.zh: 初，英兵在定海，殘虐人民，既退，猶四出遊奕。

translations.literal: At first, when British troops were at Dinghai, they cruelly abused the people; even after withdrawing, they still ranged about on patrol in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while British troops held Dinghai, they had brutalized the local population; even after withdrawing, they continued to roam the area on patrol.

sentences.zh: 裕謙捕獲兵目，剝皮抽筋而懸之，又掘敵屍焚於通衢。

translations.literal: Yu Qian captured enemy soldiers, flayed and dismembered them and hung them up, and also dug up enemy corpses and burned them in the public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian captured enemy soldiers, flayed and dismembered them and hung their bodies on display, and also dug up enemy corpses and burned them in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 英人遂藉口復仇，大舉再犯浙洋，裕謙率江寧駐防及徐州鎮兵千，馳至鎮海督戰，令總兵葛雲飛、鄭國鴻、王錫朋率兵五千守定海，手緘密諭，付臨陣啟視，退者立斬。

translations.literal: The English then used this as a pretext for revenge and launched a major renewed attack on the Zhejiang seas; Yu Qian led a thousand troops from the Jiangning garrison and Xuzhou garrison, hurried to Zhenhai to direct the battle, and ordered commanding generals Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, and Wang Xipeng to lead five thousand men to hold Dinghai, sealing secret orders by hand to be opened only in battle, with immediate execution for any who retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The British then used this as a pretext for revenge and launched a major new offensive in Zhejiang waters; Yu Qian led a thousand men from the Jiangning and Xuzhou garrisons to Zhenhai to direct the fighting, and ordered Ge Yunfei, Zheng Guohong, and Wang Xipeng to hold Dinghai with five thousand troops, handing them sealed orders to be opened only in battle and decreeing instant execution for anyone who retreated.

sentences.zh: 八月，敵艦二十九艘、兵三萬來攻，分三路並進，血戰六晝夜，三鎮並死之，定海陷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, twenty-nine enemy warships and thirty thousand troops came to attack, advancing in three columns simultaneously; after six days and nights of bloody fighting, all three commanding generals died and Dinghai fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, twenty-nine enemy warships and thirty thousand troops attacked in three columns; after six days and nights of bloody fighting, all three commanding generals were killed and Dinghai fell.

sentences.zh: 越數日，敵由蛟門島進犯鎮海，招寶山為要衝，餘步雲守之，別遣總兵謝朝恩守金雞嶺為犄角。

translations.literal: Several days later, the enemy advanced from Jiaomen Island to attack Zhenhai; Zhaobaoshan was the strategic point, which Yu Buyun defended, while commanding general Xie Chaoen was separately dispatched to hold Jinji Ridge as a supporting position.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the enemy advanced from Jiaomen Island against Zhenhai; Yu Buyun held Zhaobaoshan, the key position, while Xie Chaoen was posted at Jinji Ridge to support him.

sentences.zh: 裕謙疑步雲懷兩端，乃集將士祭關帝、天后，與眾約：「毋以退守為詞，離城一步；

translations.literal: Yu Qian suspected Yu Buyun of double-dealing, so he gathered officers and soldiers to offer sacrifice to Lord Guan and the Queen of Heaven, and made a covenant with the assembly: "Do not use retreat as an excuse to leave the city by a single step;
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting Yu Buyun of wavering, Yu Qian gathered the officers and men to offer sacrifice to Lord Guan and the Queen of Heaven and bound them with an oath: "Do not use retreat as an excuse to leave the city by even a single step;

sentences.zh: 亦毋以保全民命為詞，受洋人片紙。

translations.literal: nor use saving the people's lives as an excuse to accept a single slip of paper from the foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: nor use protecting the people's lives as an excuse to accept any note from the foreigners.

sentences.zh: 不用命者，明正典刑，幽遭神殛！」

translations.literal: Whoever disobeys shall be publicly punished by law and secretly struck down by the gods!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever disobeys shall be punished by law in this world and struck down by the gods in the next!"

sentences.zh: 步雲知其意，不預盟誓。

translations.literal: Yu Buyun understood his meaning and did not join the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Buyun understood what Yu Qian meant and refused to take the oath.

sentences.zh: 及戰，裕謙登城，手援枹鼓，步雲詣請遣外委陳志剛赴敵艦，暫示羈縻，裕謙不許。

translations.literal: When battle came, Yu Qian mounted the wall and personally beat the drum; Yu Buyun came to request that sub-official Chen Zhigang be sent to the enemy ships to show temporary restraint, but Yu Qian would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When battle came, Yu Qian mounted the wall and beat the war drum himself; Yu Buyun came to ask that sub-official Chen Zhigang be sent to the enemy ships as a temporary delaying gesture, but Yu Qian refused.

sentences.zh: 有頃，敵登招寶山，步云不戰而退。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy scaled Zhaobaoshan, and Yu Buyun withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy scaled Zhaobaoshan, and Yu Buyun retreated without a fight.

sentences.zh: 敵復分兵攻金雞嶺，謝朝恩中砲殞，兩山同陷，鎮海守兵望風而潰。

translations.literal: The enemy then divided forces to attack Jinji Ridge; Xie Chaoen was struck by cannon fire and killed, both hills fell together, and the Zhenhai garrison fled at the sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then sent a detachment against Jinji Ridge; Xie Chaoen was killed by cannon fire, both hills fell together, and the Zhenhai garrison fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 裕謙先誓必死，一日經學宮前，見泮池石鐫「流芳」二字，曰：「他日於此收吾屍也！

translations.literal: Yu Qian had earlier sworn to die; one day as he passed before the Confucian academy, he saw the characters "lasting fame" carved on a stone by the Pan Pool and said: "One day my corpse will be collected here!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian had already sworn to die rather than surrender; one day, passing the Confucian academy, he saw the characters "lasting fame" carved on a stone by the Pan Pool and said, "One day my body will be recovered here!

sentences.zh: 吾曾祖於乾隆二十一年八月殉難，今值道光二十一年八月，非佳兆。」

translations.literal: My great-grandfather died in martyrdom in the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Qianlong; now it is the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Daoguang—not a good omen."
translations.idiomatic: My great-grandfather died in battle in the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Qianlong, and now it is the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Daoguang—not a good omen."

sentences.zh: 預檢硃批寄諭、奏稿送嘉興行館，處分家事甚悉。

translations.literal: He had already sorted out imperial rescripts, transmitted orders, and memorial drafts and sent them to his lodge at Jiaxing, settling his household affairs in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: He had already sorted out the emperor's rescripts, transmitted orders, and memorial drafts and sent them to his lodge at Jiaxing, putting his household affairs in order in meticulous detail.

sentences.zh: 臨戰，揮幕客先去，曰：「勝，為我草露布；

translations.literal: On the eve of battle he sent his secretaries away first, saying: "If we win, draft a victory proclamation for me;
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle he sent his secretaries away, saying, "If we win, draft a victory proclamation for me;

sentences.zh: 敗，則代辦後事。」

translations.literal: if we lose, then handle my affairs after death."
translations.idiomatic: if we lose, then see to my affairs after death."

sentences.zh: 至是果投泮​​池，副將豐伸泰等拯之出，輿至府城，昏憊不省人事。

translations.literal: At this point he indeed threw himself into the Pan Pool; Vice General Feng Shentai and others rescued him, carried him in a litter to the prefectural city, where he lay unconscious in exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: When defeat came he did indeed throw himself into the Pan Pool; Vice General Feng Shentai and others pulled him out and carried him in a litter to the prefectural city, where he lay unconscious and near death.

sentences.zh: 敵且至，以小舟載往餘姚，卒於途，遂至西興，劉韻珂等視其斂。

translations.literal: As the enemy was about to arrive, he was carried in a small boat toward Yuyao and died on the way; his body was then taken to Xixing, where Liu Yunke and others oversaw his encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy approaching, he was carried by small boat toward Yuyao but died on the way; his body was taken on to Xixing, where Liu Yunke and others oversaw his encoffining.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子太保，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，附祀京師昭忠祠，於鎮海建立專祠，諡靖節。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, awarded a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry together with one of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, enshrined in the Capital Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, granted a dedicated shrine at Zhenhai, and given the posthumous title Jingjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry; he was enshrined in the Capital Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, given a dedicated shrine at Zhenhai, and posthumously titled Jingjie.

sentences.zh: 柩至京，遣成郡王載銳奠醊。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, Prince Cheng Zai Rui was dispatched to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin reached the capital, Prince Cheng Zai Rui was sent to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 當初敗，餘步雲疏報鎮海大營先潰，裕謙不知所往。

translations.literal: At the first defeat, Yu Buyun reported in a memorial that the main camp at Zhenhai had collapsed first and that Yu Qian's whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Immediately after the defeat, Yu Buyun reported that the main camp at Zhenhai had broken first and that Yu Qian's whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 韻珂等奏至，上始釋疑，予優恤。

translations.literal: When Yunke's memorial arrived, the emperor's suspicions were finally dispelled and exceptional posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yunke's memorial arrived, the emperor's suspicions were finally laid to rest and exceptional honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 幕客陳若木從兵間代裕謙妻草狀，詣闕訟冤，逮步雲論治伏法。

translations.literal: The secretary Chen Ruomu, amid the chaos of battle, drafted a petition on behalf of Yu Qian's wife, went to the capital to plead for redress, and Yu Buyun was arrested, tried, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian's secretary Chen Ruomu, amid the chaos of battle, drafted a petition on behalf of Yu Qian's wife and went to the capital to seek redress; Yu Buyun was arrested, tried, and executed.

sentences.zh: 嗣子德崚襲世職，以主事用，官至山東候補知府。

translations.literal: His successor son Deling inherited the hereditary office, was employed as a principal secretary, and rose to acting prefect of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deling inherited the hereditary rank, entered service as a principal secretary, and eventually rose to acting prefect of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 謝朝恩，四川華陽人。

translations.literal: Xie Chaoen, a native of Huayang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chaoen was a native of Huayang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由行伍從將軍德楞泰剿教匪，積功至都司。

translations.literal: From the ranks he followed General Delengtai in suppressing the sect rebels, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks, following General Delengtai in suppressing the sect rebels, and accumulated enough merit to reach the rank of colonel.

sentences.zh: 累擢閩浙督標副將，從平台灣張丙亂。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice general of the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general's banner and took part in suppressing Zhang Bing's rebellion at Pingtan Bay.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to vice general of the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general's banner and took part in suppressing Zhang Bing's rebellion at Pingtan Bay.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年，擢狼山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Daoguang he was promoted to commanding general of Langshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Daoguang he was promoted to commanding general of Langshan.

sentences.zh: 從伊里布防鎮海，充翼長。

translations.literal: He followed Yilibu in defending Zhenhai and served as wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yilibu in defending Zhenhai and served as wing commander.

sentences.zh: 裕謙令守金雞嶺，力戰禦敵。

translations.literal: Yu Qian ordered him to hold Jinji Ridge, where he fought hard to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian ordered him to hold Jinji Ridge, where he fought fiercely to repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵別出一隊由沙蟹嶺繞出山後夾攻，遙見招寶山威遠城已為敵踞，兵遂潰。

translations.literal: The enemy sent a separate detachment around from behind via Shaxie Ridge to attack from both sides; from afar he saw that Weiyuan City on Zhaobaoshan had already been seized by the enemy, and the troops then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent a separate detachment around Shaxie Ridge to attack from the rear; seeing from afar that Weiyuan City on Zhaobaoshan had already fallen, his troops broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 朝恩扼砲台，中敵砲，墮海，屍不獲。

translations.literal: Chaoen held the battery but was struck by enemy cannon fire, fell into the sea, and his body was never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen held the battery but was struck by enemy cannon fire, fell into the sea, and his body was never recovered.

sentences.zh: 浙人有親見其死者，歌詠傳其事，與葛雲飛等同稱四鎮雲。

translations.literal: People of Zhejiang who had witnessed his death sang and recited poems spreading his story, and together with Ge Yunfei and the others he was called one of the Four Zhen Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang locals who had witnessed his death sang poems to spread his story, and together with Ge Yunfei and the others he came to be known as one of the Four Zhen Generals.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Posthumous relief was granted and a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors were granted, including a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 重祥，張氏，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhong Xiang, of the Zhang clan, a Han Bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Xiang, of the Zhang clan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 世襲一等輕車都尉，金華協副將。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary office of Commandant of Light Chariots of the first rank and served as vice general of the Jinhua garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary rank of first-class Commandant of Light Chariots and served as vice general of the Jinhua garrison.

sentences.zh: 從葛雲飛戰定海受傷，复佐守金雞嶺，力戰死之。

translations.literal: He fought at Dinghai under Ge Yunfei and was wounded, then again assisted in holding Jinji Ridge and died fighting hard.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Dinghai under Ge Yunfei and was wounded, then helped defend Jinji Ridge and died fighting there.

sentences.zh: 處州營游擊托雲保，卞氏，亦漢軍旗人，偕重祥同殞於陣，並予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Tuoyunbao, a battalion commander of the Chuzhou garrison of the Bian clan, also a Han Bannerman, died together with Zhong Xiang on the battlefield, and both were granted hereditary offices of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoyunbao, a battalion commander of the Chuzhou garrison and a Han Bannerman of the Bian clan, died alongside Zhong Xiang in battle, and both were granted hereditary ranks of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 關天培，字滋圃，江蘇山陽人。

translations.literal: Guan Tianpei, style name Zipu, a native of Shanyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Tianpei, styled Zipu, was a native of Shanyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 由行伍洊升太湖營水師副將。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was repeatedly promoted to vice admiral of the naval forces of the Taihu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to vice admiral of the Taihu garrison's naval forces.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，初行海運，督護百四十餘艘抵天津，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, when sea transport was first instituted, he supervised and escorted more than one hundred forty vessels to Tianjin and received special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang, when sea transport was first instituted, he supervised and escorted more than one hundred forty vessels to Tianjin and received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢蘇松鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to commanding general of Su-Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to commanding general of Su-Song.

sentences.zh: 十三年，署江南提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he acted as commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he served as acting commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授廣東水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed admiral of the Guangdong naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed admiral of the Guangdong naval forces.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利通商漸萌跋扈，兵船闌入內河，前提督李增階以疏防黜，天培代之。

translations.literal: At the time England's trade was gradually growing overbearing; warships intruded into the inner rivers, and the previous admiral Li Zengjie was dismissed for lax defense; Tianpei replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: England's traders were growing increasingly arrogant, and warships were intruding into the inner rivers; the previous admiral Li Zengjie had been dismissed for lax defense, and Tianpei replaced him.

sentences.zh: 至則親歷海洋阨塞，增修虎門、南山、橫檔諸砲台，鑄六千斤大砲四十座，請籌操練犒賞經費。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he personally inspected the strategic points on the seas, added and repaired the batteries at Humen, Nanshan, Hengdang, and elsewhere, cast forty six-thousand-jin great guns, and requested funds for training and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he personally inspected the strategic points at sea, strengthened the forts at Humen, Nanshan, Hengdang, and elsewhere, cast forty six-thousand-jin cannons, and requested funds for training and rewards.

sentences.zh: 十八年，英人馬他倫至澳門，託言稽察商務，投函不如製，天培卻之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Englishman Maitland reached Macau, claiming to inspect commercial affairs; his letter did not follow proper form, and Tianpei rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Englishman Maitland reached Macau, claiming to inspect commercial affairs; his letter did not follow proper protocol, and Tianpei rejected it.

sentences.zh: 禁煙事起，偕總督鄧廷楨偵緝甚力。

translations.literal: When the opium prohibition began, together with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen he pursued detection and seizure with great vigor.
translations.idiomatic: When the opium prohibition campaign began, he worked closely with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen to hunt down smugglers with great vigor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，林則徐蒞廣東，檄天培勒躉船繳煙二萬餘箱焚之，於是嚴海防，橫檔山前海面較狹可扼，鑄巨鐵練橫系之二重，阻敵舟不能迳過，砲台乃得以伺擊。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong and ordered Tianpei to compel the hulks to surrender more than twenty thousand chests of opium for burning; thereafter sea defenses were tightened; the waters before Hengdang Mountain were relatively narrow and could be held, so huge iron chains were cast and stretched across in two rows to block enemy vessels from passing directly, allowing the batteries to strike at will.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong and ordered Tianpei to compel the hulks to surrender more than twenty thousand chests of opium for burning; sea defenses were then tightened; the waters before Hengdang Mountain were narrow enough to block, so huge iron chains were cast and stretched across in two rows to prevent enemy vessels from passing directly, allowing the forts to strike at will.

sentences.zh: 則徐倚天培如左右手，常駐沙角，督本標及陽江、碣石兩鎮師船排日操練。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu relied on Tianpei as on his right and left hands; Tianpei constantly stationed himself at Shajiao, supervising the flagship and the squadrons of the Yangjiang and Jieshi garrisons in daily drill.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu relied on Tianpei as his right hand; Tianpei constantly stationed himself at Shajiao, supervising the flagship and the squadrons of the Yangjiang and Jieshi garrisons in daily drill.

sentences.zh: 七月，英艦突犯九龍山口，為參將賴恩爵擊退。

translations.literal: In the seventh month British warships suddenly attacked Jiulongshan Pass and were repelled by Colonel Lai Enjue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month British warships suddenly attacked Jiulongshan Pass and were repelled by Colonel Lai Enjue.

sentences.zh: 九月，二艦至穿鼻洋，阻商船進口，挑戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month two warships reached Chuanbi Bay, blocked merchant ships from entering port, and issued a challenge.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month two warships reached Chuanbi Bay, blocked merchant ships from entering port, and issued a challenge.

sentences.zh: 天培身立桅前，拔刀督陣，退者立斬。

translations.literal: Tianpei stood himself before the mast, drew his sword to direct the battle line, and ordered immediate execution for any who retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei stood at the mast, drew his sword to direct the battle line, and decreed instant execution for anyone who retreated.

sentences.zh: 有擊中敵船一砲者，立予重賞，發砲破敵船頭鼻，敵紛紛落海，乃遁。

translations.literal: Whoever struck an enemy ship with one cannon shot was immediately given a heavy reward; cannon fire broke the enemy ship's bow, the enemy fell into the sea one after another, and they then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who struck an enemy ship with a single cannon shot was immediately given a heavy reward; cannon fire shattered an enemy ship's bow, the enemy fell into the sea one after another, and they fled.

sentences.zh: 敵艦久泊尖沙嘴，踞為巢穴。

translations.literal: Enemy warships had long anchored at Tsim Sha Tsui and occupied it as a nest.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy warships had long anchored at Tsim Sha Tsui and made it their base.

sentences.zh: 迤北山梁曰官湧，俯視聚泊之所，攻擊最便，天培增砲駐營，敵屢乘隙來爭，不得逞。

translations.literal: The ridge to the north called Guanyong overlooked the anchorage and was most convenient for attack; Tianpei added guns and stationed troops there, and though the enemy repeatedly seized openings to contest it, they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The ridge to the north, called Guanyong, overlooked the anchorage and was ideal for attack; Tianpei added guns and stationed troops there, and though the enemy repeatedly tried to seize it, they could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 十月，敵以大艦正面來攻，小舟載兵從側乘潮撲岸，殲之於山岡；

translations.literal: In the tenth month the enemy attacked head-on with large warships while small boats carried troops to rush ashore on the flank with the tide; they were annihilated on the hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the enemy attacked head-on with large warships while small boats carried troops ashore on the flank with the tide; they were wiped out on the hills.

sentences.zh: 复於迤東胡椒角窺伺，砲擊走之。

translations.literal: Again they spied from Huajiao to the east and were driven off by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: They also tried to probe from Huajiao to the east and were driven off by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 乃調集水陸兵守山梁，參將陳連升、賴恩爵、張斌，游擊伍通標、德連等為五路，合同進攻。

translations.literal: He then gathered land and naval forces to hold the ridge, with Colonels Chen Liansheng, Lai Enjue, and Zhang Bin and battalion commanders Wu Tongbiao, Delian, and others forming five columns for a combined advance.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered land and naval forces to hold the ridge, with Colonels Chen Liansheng, Lai Enjue, and Zhang Bin and battalion commanders Wu Tongbiao and Delian forming five columns for a combined assault.

sentences.zh: 敵乘夜來犯，五路大砲齊擊，敵舟自撞，燈火皆滅。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked by night; the five columns' great guns fired together, enemy vessels collided with one another, and all lights went out.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy attacked by night; the five columns' great guns fired together, enemy vessels collided with one another, and all their lights went out.

sentences.zh: 侵曉瞭望，逃者過半，僅存十餘舟遠泊。

translations.literal: At dawn on inspection, more than half had fled, and only a dozen or so vessels remained anchored far off.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn more than half had fled, and only a dozen or so vessels remained anchored far off.

sentences.zh: 次日，復有二敵艦潛進，隨者十數，复諸路合擊，毀其頭船，遂散泊外洋。

translations.literal: The next day two more enemy warships slipped in with a dozen or so followers; again all columns combined in attack, destroyed the lead ship, and they then scattered to anchor in the outer seas.
translations.idiomatic: The next day two more enemy warships slipped in with about a dozen followers; again all columns combined in attack, destroyed the lead ship, and the rest scattered to anchor in the outer seas.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎，賜號法福靈阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When word of victory reached the court, an edict commended him and granted the title Fafu Ling'a Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When word of victory reached the court, an edict commended him and granted him the title Fafu Ling'a Batulu.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，英艦雖不敢復進，猶招奸民​​分路載煙私售。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year, though British warships dared not advance again, they still recruited corrupt locals to carry opium by separate routes for private sale.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year, though British warships dared not advance again, they still recruited corrupt locals to smuggle opium by separate routes for private sale.

sentences.zh: 天培沿海搜捕，一日數起，复飭漁船蟹艇乘間焚毀敵舟，英人始改計他犯。

translations.literal: Tianpei searched and seized along the coast, with several cases in a single day; he also ordered fishing boats and crab skiffs to seize openings to burn and destroy enemy vessels, and only then did the English change plans to attack elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei searched and seized along the coast, with several cases in a single day; he also ordered fishing boats and crab skiffs to seize openings to burn enemy vessels, and only then did the British change plans and attack elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 及林則徐罷，琦善代之，一意主撫，至粵，先撤沿海防禦，僅留水師制兵三分之一，募勇盡散，而英人要索甚奢，久無定議，戰釁復起。

translations.literal: When Lin Zexu was dismissed, Qishan replaced him and was bent solely on conciliation; upon reaching Guangdong, he first withdrew coastal defenses, leaving only one-third of the naval regular troops, disbanded all hired braves, yet the English demands were extremely extravagant and no agreement was reached for a long time, and the spark of war flared again.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Zexu was dismissed and Qishan replaced him, Qishan was bent solely on conciliation; upon reaching Guangdong he first withdrew the coastal defenses, leaving only one-third of the naval regular troops and disbanding all hired braves, yet the British demands were extravagant and no agreement could be reached for a long time, and war broke out again.

sentences.zh: 十二月，英船攻虎門外沙角砲台，副將陳連升死之，大角砲台隨陷，並為敵踞，虎門危急。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, English ships attacked the Shajiao battery outside Humen; Vice General Chen Liansheng died, the Dajiao battery then fell, and both were seized by the enemy; Humen was in grave peril.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, British ships attacked the Shajiao battery outside Humen; Vice General Chen Liansheng was killed, the Dajiao battery then fell, and both were seized by the enemy; Humen was in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 天培與總兵李廷鈺分守靖遠、威遠兩砲台，請援，琦善僅遣兵二百。

translations.literal: Tianpei and commanding general Li Tingyu separately defended the Jingyuan and Weiyuan batteries, requested reinforcements, and Qishan sent only two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei and commanding general Li Tingyu held the Jingyuan and Weiyuan batteries respectively; they requested reinforcements, but Qishan sent only two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，敵進攻，守台兵僅數百，遣將慟哭請益師，無應者。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year the enemy advanced to attack; the garrison numbered only a few hundred; dispatched officers wept and begged for more troops, but none responded.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-first year the enemy attacked; the garrison numbered only a few hundred; officers sent to plead for reinforcements wept in despair, but no help came.

sentences.zh: 天培度眾寡不敵，乃決以死守，出私財餉將士，率游擊麥廷章晝夜督戰。

translations.literal: Tianpei judged that his forces were too few to match the enemy and resolved to die defending to the last; he paid the officers and soldiers from his private funds and led battalion commander Mai Tingzhang in directing the battle day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his forces were too few to match the enemy, Tianpei resolved to die defending to the last; he paid the officers and men from his own purse and led battalion commander Mai Tingzhang in directing the battle day and night.

sentences.zh: 敵入三門口，衝斷椿練，奮擊甫退，南風大作，敵船大隊圍橫檔、永安兩砲台，遂陷。

translations.literal: The enemy entered Sanmenkou, broke through the piles and chains, and were driven back only after fierce fighting; then a strong south wind arose, a large enemy fleet surrounded the Hengdang and Yong'an batteries, and they fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy entered Sanmenkou, broke through the piles and chains, and were driven back only after fierce fighting; then a strong south wind arose, a large enemy fleet surrounded the Hengdang and Yong'an batteries, and both fell.

sentences.zh: 進攻虎門，自巳至酉，殺傷相當，而砲門透水不得發，敵自台後攢擊，身被數十創。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack on Humen from the si hour to the you hour; casualties were roughly equal, but water seeped into the gun ports so the guns could not fire; the enemy attacked in a mass from behind the battery, and he received several dozen wounds.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack on Humen from mid-morning to evening; casualties were roughly equal, but water seeped into the gun ports so the guns could not fire; the enemy attacked in force from behind the battery, and he received dozens of wounds.

sentences.zh: 事急，以印投僕孫長慶，令去，行未遠，回顧天培已殞絕於地，廷章亦同死，砲台遂陷。

translations.literal: When matters grew urgent, he handed his seal to his servant Sun Changqing and ordered him to leave; he had not gone far when he looked back and saw Tianpei already fallen dead on the ground; Tingzhang also died together, and the battery then fell.
translations.idiomatic: When matters grew desperate, he handed his seal to his servant Sun Changqing and ordered him to leave; Sun had not gone far when he looked back and saw Tianpei already fallen dead on the ground; Tingzhang also died, and the battery fell.

sentences.zh: 長慶縋崖出，繳印於總督，復往尋天培屍，半體焦焉，負以出。

translations.literal: Changqing lowered himself down the cliff by rope, surrendered the seal to the governor-general, then went back to search for Tianpei's corpse; half the body was charred, and he carried it out on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing lowered himself down the cliff by rope, surrendered the seal to the governor-general, then went back to search for Tianpei's body; half of it was charred, and he carried it out on his back.

sentences.zh: 優恤，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡忠節，入祀昭忠祠，建立專祠。

translations.literal: Exceptional posthumous honors were granted; he was awarded a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry together with one of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, given the posthumous title Zhongjie, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and granted a dedicated shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptional posthumous honors were granted; he was awarded hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, posthumously titled Zhongjie, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and granted a dedicated shrine.

sentences.zh: 母吳年逾八十，命地方官存問，給銀米以養餘年。

translations.literal: His mother Wu was over eighty years old; local officials were ordered to inquire after her welfare and provide silver and grain to support her remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Wu was over eighty; local officials were ordered to inquire after her welfare and provide silver and grain to support her in her remaining years.

sentences.zh: 子從龍襲世職，官安徽候補同知。

translations.literal: His son Conglong inherited the hereditary office and served as acting sub-prefect of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Conglong inherited the hereditary rank and served as acting sub-prefect of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 陳連升，湖北鶴峰人。

translations.literal: Chen Liansheng, a native of Hefeng in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liansheng was a native of Hefeng in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 由行伍從征川、楚、陝教匪，湖南、廣東逆瑤，數有功。

translations.literal: From the ranks he campaigned against the sect rebels in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi and against the rebellious Yao in Hunan and Guangdong, achieving merit on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks, campaigning against the sect rebels in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi and against the rebellious Yao in Hunan and Guangdong, and won distinction on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 累擢增城營參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to colonel of the Zengcheng garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to colonel of the Zengcheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光十九年，破英兵於官湧，擢三江協副將，調守沙角砲台。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang he defeated English troops at Guanyong, was promoted to vice general of the Sanjiang garrison, and was transferred to defend the Shajiao battery.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Daoguang he defeated British troops at Guanyong, was promoted to vice general of the Sanjiang garrison, and was transferred to defend the Shajiao battery.

sentences.zh: 及英艦來犯，連升率子武舉長鵬以兵六百當敵數千，發地雷扛砲斃敵數百，卒無援，歿於陣，長鵬赴水死。

translations.literal: When English warships came to attack, Liansheng led his son Changpeng, a military licentiate, with six hundred men to face several thousand enemy troops; they detonated land mines and fired great guns, killing several hundred enemy soldiers, but in the end there was no relief and he died on the battlefield; Changpeng drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: When British warships attacked, Liansheng led his son Changpeng, a military licentiate, with six hundred men against several thousand enemy troops; they detonated land mines and fired great guns, killing hundreds of the enemy, but no relief came and he died on the battlefield; Changpeng drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 敵以連升戰最猛，臠其屍。

translations.literal: Because Liansheng had fought most fiercely, the enemy mutilated his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liansheng had fought most fiercely, the enemy mutilated his body.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔嘉其父子忠孝兩全，入祀昭忠祠，並建專祠，加等依總兵例賜卹，予騎都尉世職，子展鵬襲，起鵬賜舉人。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, an edict commended father and son for fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety, enshrined them in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, granted a dedicated shrine, awarded posthumous honors by the standard for commanding generals with an added grade, granted a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, which son Zhanpeng inherited, and Qipeng was granted the rank of licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict commended father and son for fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety; they were enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness and granted a dedicated shrine; posthumous honors were awarded by the standard for commanding generals with an added grade; a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry was granted, which son Zhanpeng inherited, and Qipeng was granted the rank of licentiate.

sentences.zh: 祥福，瑪佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Xiang Fu, of the Majia clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Fu, of the Majia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由親軍累擢冠軍使。

translations.literal: From the imperial guard he was repeatedly promoted to Champion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the imperial guard to be promoted repeatedly to Champion.

sentences.zh: 出為湖南寶慶協副將。

translations.literal: He was sent out as vice general of the Baoqing garrison in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as vice general of the Baoqing garrison in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 從提督羅思舉平江華瑤有功。

translations.literal: He followed Admiral Luo Siju in pacifying the Jianghua Yao and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Admiral Luo Siju in pacifying the Jianghua Yao and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 歷綏靖、寧夏、鎮筸諸鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He served successively as commanding general of Suijing, Ningxia, and Zhenqian.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as commanding general of Suijing, Ningxia, and Zhenqian.

sentences.zh: 二十年，率本鎮兵援廣東。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he led troops from his garrison to reinforce Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he led troops from his garrison to reinforce Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，守烏湧砲台，與虎門同時陷，祥福死之，予騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he defended the Wuyong battery; it fell at the same time as Humen, and Xiang Fu died; a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded and he was enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he defended the Wuyong battery; it fell at the same time as Humen, and Xiang Fu was killed; he was granted a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry and enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 尋詔與關天培同建專祠。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered that a dedicated shrine be built jointly with Guan Tianpei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered that a dedicated shrine be built jointly with Guan Tianpei.

sentences.zh: 子喜瀛，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Xiying inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiying inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 天培等皆以琦善不欲戰，無援，故敗，海內傷之，而福建總兵江繼芸又以顏伯燾促戰而亡。

translations.literal: Tianpei and the others all failed because Qishan did not wish to fight and sent no relief; the whole realm grieved for them, while Fujian commanding general Jiang Jiyun also died because Yan Bozhan pressed for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Tianpei and the others all failed because Qishan did not wish to fight and sent no relief; the whole realm grieved for them, while Fujian commanding general Jiang Jiyun also died because Yan Bozhan pressed for battle.

sentences.zh: 繼芸，福建平潭人。

translations.literal: Jiyun, a native of Pingtan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun was a native of Pingtan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由行伍拔補千總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was selected and appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to be appointed company commander.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，台灣張丙之亂，戰枋樹窩、小雞籠，以擒賊功擢守備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, during Zhang Bing's rebellion in Taiwan, he fought at Fangshuwo and Xiaojilong and was promoted to battalion commander for merit in capturing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang, during Zhang Bing's rebellion in Taiwan, he fought at Fangshuwo and Xiaojilong and was promoted to battalion commander for capturing rebels.

sentences.zh: 累遷台灣副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred and promoted to vice general of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to vice general of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，署南澳鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he acted as commanding general of Nan'ao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he served as acting commanding general of Nan'ao.

sentences.zh: 總督鄧廷楨薦其才，尋擢海壇鎮總兵，調金​​門鎮，從顏伯燾守廈門。

translations.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen recommended his talent; soon he was promoted to commanding general of Haitan, transferred to the Jinmen garrison, and followed Yan Bozhan in defending Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen recommended his talent; he was soon promoted to commanding general of Haitan, transferred to the Jinmen garrison, and joined Yan Bozhan in defending Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廣東方議款，英艦遊奕閩洋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, while Guangdong was negotiating a settlement, English warships prowled the Fujian seas.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, while Guangdong was negotiating a settlement, British warships prowled the Fujian seas.

sentences.zh: 伯燾素主戰，庀船砲備出擊，而新裁水勇未散，軍心不堅，繼芸以為言，伯燾不聽。

translations.literal: Bozhan had always favored war and prepared ships and guns for an attack, but newly dismissed naval braves had not yet dispersed and army morale was unsteady; Jiyun spoke of this, but Bozhan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhan had always favored war and prepared ships and guns for an attack, but newly dismissed naval braves had not yet dispersed and army morale was shaky; Jiyun raised the point, but Bozhan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 七月，英艦泊鼓浪嶼，集水陸師禦諸嶼口，砲毀敵舟，而敵已撲砲台登岸，陸師先潰，繼芸急赴援，中砲落海死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month English warships anchored at Gulangyu; land and naval forces were gathered to defend the island passes; cannon fire destroyed enemy vessels, but the enemy had already rushed the battery and landed; the land forces collapsed first; Jiyun hurried to reinforce but was struck by cannon fire, fell into the sea, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month British warships anchored at Gulangyu; land and naval forces were gathered to defend the island passes and cannon fire destroyed enemy vessels, but the enemy had already rushed the battery and landed; the land forces broke first; Jiyun hurried to reinforce but was struck by cannon fire, fell into the sea, and died.

sentences.zh: 護理延平協副將凌志、淮口都司王世俊同殉。

translations.literal: Acting vice general of the Yanping garrison Ling Zhi and Huai Pass commander Wang Shijun died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Acting vice general of the Yanping garrison Ling Zhi and Huai Pass commander Wang Shijun died alongside him.

sentences.zh: 凌志，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Ling Zhi, of the Fuca clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zhi, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 陳化成，字蓮峰，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Chen Huacheng, style name Lianfeng, a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huacheng, styled Lianfeng, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由行伍授水師把總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was appointed company commander of the naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to be appointed company commander of the naval forces.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，從提督李長庚擊蔡牽，數有功，以勇聞。

translations.literal: During the Jiaqing reign he followed Admiral Li Changgeng in attacking Cai Qian, achieved merit on several occasions, and was known for his bravery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign he served under Admiral Li Changgeng in the campaign against the pirate Cai Qian, won distinction on several occasions, and was known for his bravery.

sentences.zh: 累擢烽火門參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to colonel of Fenghuomen.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to colonel of Fenghuomen.

sentences.zh: 總督董教增薦其久歷閩、粵水師，手擒巨盜四百八十餘人，勤勞最著，請補澎湖副將，以籍隸本省，格不行。

translations.literal: Governor-General Dong Jiaozeng recommended that he had long served in the Fujian and Guangdong naval forces, had personally captured more than four hundred eighty major pirates, and his diligence was most outstanding; he requested appointment as vice general of Penghu, but because his native place was in the same province, the appointment was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Dong Jiaozeng recommended him for long service in the Fujian and Guangdong naval forces, for having personally captured more than four hundred eighty major pirates, and for outstanding diligence; he requested appointment as vice general of Penghu, but because his native place was in the same province, the appointment was blocked.

sentences.zh: 遷瑞安協副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice general of the Ruian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice general of the Ruian garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，乃調澎湖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was finally transferred to Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he was finally transferred to Penghu.

sentences.zh: 歷碣石、金門兩鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He served successively as commanding general of Jieshi and Jinmen.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as commanding general of Jieshi and Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢福建水師提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to admiral of the Fujian naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to admiral of the Fujian naval forces.

sentences.zh: 十二年，英吉利船駛入閩、浙、江南、山東洋面，命化成督師巡邏，以備不虞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year English ships entered the seas off Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong; Huacheng was ordered to lead troops on patrol to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year British ships entered the seas off Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong; Huacheng was ordered to lead troops on patrol against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 同安潘塗、宦潯、柏頭諸鄉素為盜藪，掩捕悉平之。

translations.literal: The villages of Pantu, Huanxun, and Botou in Tong'an had long been pirate haunts; he conducted surprise arrests and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: The villages of Pantu, Huanxun, and Botou in Tong'an had long been pirate haunts; he conducted surprise raids and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英艦犯閩，化成率師船擊之於梅林洋，尋退去。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year English warships violated Fujian; Huacheng led squadron ships to attack them at Meilin Bay, and they soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year British warships attacked Fujian; Huacheng led squadron ships to attack them at Meilin Bay, and they soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 調江南提督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 江南水師素怯懦，化成選閩中親軍教練，士氣稍振。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan naval forces had always been timid; Huacheng selected personal troops from Fujian to train them, and morale was somewhat revived.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan naval forces had always been timid; Huacheng selected personal troops from Fujian to train them, and morale revived somewhat.

sentences.zh: 籌備吳淞防務，修台鑄砲，沿海塘築二十六堡。

translations.literal: He prepared the defenses of Wusong, repaired batteries and cast guns, and built twenty-six forts along the coastal embankments.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared the defenses of Wusong, repaired batteries and cast guns, and built twenty-six forts along the coastal embankments.

sentences.zh: 化成枕戈海上凡二年，與士卒同勞苦，風雨寒暑不避，總督裕謙、牛鑑皆倚為長城。

translations.literal: Huacheng slept with his weapon at the ready on the seas for two years in all, sharing hardship with the soldiers, never avoiding wind, rain, cold, or heat; Governors-General Yu Qian and Niu Jian both relied on him as their great wall.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng slept with his weapon at the ready on the seas for two full years, sharing hardship with his soldiers and never avoiding wind, rain, cold, or heat; Governors-General Yu Qian and Niu Jian both relied on him as their bulwark.

sentences.zh: 當定海三總兵戰歿，裕謙亦殉，化成哭之慟，謂所部曰：「武臣死於疆場，幸也。

translations.literal: When the three commanding generals at Dinghai died in battle and Yu Qian also died in martyrdom, Huacheng wept bitterly and said to his troops: "For a military officer to die on the battlefield is fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the three commanding generals at Dinghai were killed in battle and Yu Qian also died, Huacheng wept bitterly and told his troops, "For a military officer to die on the battlefield is a blessing.

sentences.zh: 汝曹勉之！」

translations.literal: You must exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: You must do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 吳淞口以東西砲台為犄角，化成率參將周世榮守西台，參將崔吉瑞、游擊董永清守東台，而徐州鎮王志元守小沙背，以防繞襲。

translations.literal: At Wusong the eastern and western batteries formed supporting positions; Huacheng led Colonel Zhou Shirong to hold the western battery, Colonels Cui Jirui and battalion commander Dong Yongqing to hold the eastern battery, and Wang Zhiyuan of the Xuzhou garrison to hold Xiaoshabei to guard against a flanking attack.
translations.idiomatic: At Wusong the eastern and western batteries formed supporting positions; Huacheng led Colonel Zhou Shirong to hold the western battery, Colonels Cui Jirui and battalion commander Dong Yongqing to hold the eastern battery, and Wang Zhiyuan of the Xuzhou garrison to hold Xiaoshabei against a flanking attack.

sentences.zh: 二十二年五月，敵來犯，泊外洋，以汽舟二，列木人兩舷，繞小沙背鄉西台，欲試我效力。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year the enemy came to attack, anchored in the outer seas, and with two steam vessels lined wooden figures along both sides, circled Xiaoshabei toward the western battery, intending to test our effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-second year the enemy attacked, anchored in the outer seas, and sent two steam vessels with wooden figures lined along both sides to circle Xiaoshabei toward the western battery, intending to test the defenders' response.

sentences.zh: 化成知之，不發，敵舟旋去，以水牌浮書約戰。

translations.literal: Huacheng understood this and did not fire; the enemy vessels soon departed and floated a written challenge on a water board inviting battle.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng understood the ruse and did not fire; the enemy vessels soon departed and floated a written challenge inviting battle.

sentences.zh: 牛鑑方駐寶山，慮敵鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Niu Jian was then stationed at Baoshan and feared the enemy's momentum could not be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jian was then stationed at Baoshan and feared the enemy's momentum was unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 化成曰​​：「吾經歷海洋四十餘年，在砲彈中入死出生，難以數計。

translations.literal: Huacheng said: "I have spent more than forty years on the seas, passing in and out of death amid cannon fire more times than can be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Huacheng said, "I have spent more than forty years on the seas, passing in and out of death amid cannon fire more times than I can count.

sentences.zh: 今見敵勿擊，是畏敵也。

translations.literal: To see the enemy now and not strike is to fear the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: To see the enemy and not strike is to fear them.

sentences.zh: 奉命討賊，有進無退。

translations.literal: Ordered to suppress the rebels, one advances and does not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to suppress the enemy, we advance and do not retreat.

sentences.zh: 扼險可勝，公勿怖！」

translations.literal: Hold the strategic points and victory is possible—Your Excellency, do not be afraid!"
translations.idiomatic: Hold the strategic points and we can win—Your Excellency, do not be afraid!"

sentences.zh: 鑑乃以化成心如鐵石，士卒用命，民情固結入告，詔特嘉之。

translations.literal: Jian then reported that Huacheng's heart was like iron and stone, the soldiers obeyed orders, and popular sentiment was firmly united; an edict specially commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jian then reported that Huacheng's resolve was like iron, the soldiers obeyed orders, and popular sentiment was firmly united; an edict specially commended him.

sentences.zh: 越數日，敵艦銜尾進，化成麾旗發砲，毀敵艦三，殲斃甚眾。

translations.literal: Several days later enemy warships advanced in close succession; Huacheng waved his flag and opened fire, destroying three enemy vessels and killing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later enemy warships advanced in close succession; Huacheng waved his flag and opened fire, destroying three enemy vessels and killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 鑑聞師得力，親至校場督戰，敵以桅砲注擊，毀演武廳，鑑遽退。

translations.literal: When Jian heard the army was gaining ground, he came in person to the drill ground to direct the battle; the enemy concentrated mast guns on him, destroyed the drill hall, and Jian hurriedly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Jian heard the army was gaining ground, he came in person to the drill ground to direct the battle; the enemy concentrated mast guns on him, destroyed the drill hall, and Niu Jian hurriedly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敵攻壞土塘，由小沙背登岸，徐州兵先奔，東台亦潰，萃攻西台，部將守備韋印福，千總錢金玉、許攀桂，外委徐大華等皆戰死。

translations.literal: The enemy broke through the earthen embankment, landed from Xiaoshabei, the Xuzhou troops fled first, the eastern battery also collapsed, and they massed to attack the western battery; subordinate officers battalion commander Wei Yinfu, company commanders Qian Jinyu and Xu Pankui, and sub-official Xu Dahua all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke through the earthen embankment and landed from Xiaoshabei; the Xuzhou troops fled first, the eastern battery also collapsed, and the enemy massed against the western battery; battalion commander Wei Yinfu, company commanders Qian Jinyu and Xu Pankui, and sub-official Xu Dahua all died fighting.

sentences.zh: 屍積於前，化成猶掬子藥親發砲，俄中彈，噴血而殞。

translations.literal: Corpses piled up before him, yet Huacheng still scooped powder and shot and fired the guns himself; soon he was struck by a bullet, spat blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses piled up before him, yet Huacheng still scooped powder and shot and fired the guns himself; soon he was struck by a bullet, spat blood, and fell dead.

sentences.zh: 砲台既失，寶山、山海相繼陷。

translations.literal: Once the battery was lost, Baoshan and Shanghai fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Once the battery was lost, Baoshan and Shanghai fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 越八日，鄉民始負其屍出，殮於嘉定。

translations.literal: After eight days the local people at last carried his corpse out and encoffined it at Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later the local people at last carried his body out and encoffined it at Jiading.

sentences.zh: 事聞，宣宗震悼，特詔優恤，賜銀一千兩治喪，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡忠愍，於殉難處所及原籍並建專祠。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, the Xuanzong Emperor was deeply shaken and grieved; a special edict granted exceptional posthumous honors, one thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses, a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry together with one of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, the posthumous title Zhongmin, and dedicated shrines at the place of martyrdom and in his native district.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Emperor Xuanzong was deeply shaken and grieved; a special edict granted exceptional posthumous honors, one thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses, hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, the posthumous title Zhongmin, and dedicated shrines at the place of his death and in his native district.

sentences.zh: 子廷芳，襲世職；

translations.literal: His son Tingfang inherited the hereditary office;
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingfang inherited the hereditary rank;

sentences.zh: 廷棻，賜舉人。

translations.literal: Tingfen was granted the rank of licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Tingfen was granted the rank of licentiate.

sentences.zh: 海齡，郭洛羅氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Hai Ling, of the Guoluoluo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hai Ling, of the Guoluoluo clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 由驍騎校授張家口守備。

translations.literal: From the rank of brave rider he was appointed battalion commander of Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: From the rank of brave rider he was appointed battalion commander of Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 累擢大名、正定兩鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to commanding general of Daming and Zhengding.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to commanding general of Daming and Zhengding.

sentences.zh: 以事降二等侍衛，充古城領隊大臣。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to second-rank imperial guardsman and appointed leading minister at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to second-rank imperial guardsman and appointed leading minister at Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 歷西安、江寧、京口副都統。

translations.literal: He served successively as Deputy Commander-in-Chief at Xi'an, Jiangning, and Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Deputy Commander-in-Chief at Xi'an, Jiangning, and Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 英兵既陷吳淞，由海入江，六月，犯鎮江，提督齊慎、劉承孝敗退，遂攻城，海齡率駐防兵死守二日，敵以雲梯入城屠旗、民，海齡與全家殉焉。

translations.literal: After English troops had captured Wusong and entered the Yangzi from the sea, in the sixth month they attacked Zhenjiang; Admirals Qi Shen and Liu Chengxiao were defeated and withdrew; the enemy then besieged the city; Hai Ling led the garrison troops in a death defense for two days; the enemy entered the city by scaling ladders and slaughtered Bannermen and civilians; Hai Ling and his entire family died in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: After British troops captured Wusong and entered the Yangzi from the sea, in the sixth month they attacked Zhenjiang; Admirals Qi Shen and Liu Chengxiao were defeated and withdrew; the enemy then besieged the city; Hai Ling led the garrison in a death defense for two days; the enemy scaled the walls and slaughtered Bannermen and civilians; Hai Ling and his entire family died.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡昭節，入祀昭忠祠，並建祠鎮江，妻及次孫附祀。

translations.literal: He was awarded a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry together with one of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, given the posthumous title Zhaojie, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, granted a shrine at Zhenjiang, and his wife and second grandson were enshrined with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, posthumously titled Zhaojie, enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and given a shrine at Zhenjiang; his wife and second grandson were enshrined with him.

sentences.zh: 當城破時，海齡禁居民不得出，常鎮道周頊棄城走，事後訐海齡妄殺良民，為眾所戕，言官亦論奏，下疆吏究勘得白，詔以闔門死難，大節無虧，仍照都統例賜卹，治頊罪如律。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Hai Ling forbade residents to leave; Chang-Zhen-Zhen circuit intendant Zhou Xu abandoned the city and fled; afterward he accused Hai Ling of wantonly killing innocent people, was killed by the crowd, and censorial officials also memorialized; frontier officials were ordered to investigate and the truth was established; an edict held that because the whole household died in martyrdom, his great integrity was unblemished, posthumous honors were still granted by the standard for deputy commanders-in-chief, and Zhou Xu was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Hai Ling forbade residents to leave; circuit intendant Zhou Xu abandoned the city and fled; afterward he accused Hai Ling of wantonly killing innocent people and was killed by the crowd; censorial officials also memorialized; frontier officials investigated and cleared Hai Ling's name; an edict held that because the whole household died in martyrdom, his great integrity was unblemished, posthumous honors were still granted by the standard for deputy commanders-in-chief, and Zhou Xu was punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 子宜蘭泰，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Yilantai inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yilantai inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 葛雲飛，字雨田，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Ge Yunfei, style name Yutian, a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Yunfei, styled Yutian, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光三年武進士，授守備，隸浙江水師。

translations.literal: A military jinshi in the third year of Daoguang, he was appointed battalion commander and attached to the Zhejiang naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: A military jinshi in the third year of Daoguang, he was appointed battalion commander in the Zhejiang naval forces.

sentences.zh: 勤於緝捕，常微服巡洋，屢獲劇盜，有名。

translations.literal: Diligent in pursuit and capture, he often patrolled in disguise and repeatedly captured major pirates, winning renown.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in pursuit and capture, he often patrolled in disguise and repeatedly captured major pirates, winning renown.

sentences.zh: 洊擢瑞安協副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice general of the Ruian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to vice general of the Ruian garrison.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署定海鎮總兵，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he acted as commanding general of Dinghai and soon received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served as acting commanding general of Dinghai and soon received the permanent appointment.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英兵犯定海，總兵張朝發戰敗失守，巡撫烏爾恭額、提督祝廷彪強起雲飛墨絰從軍，總督鄧廷楨亦薦其可倚，署定海鎮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when English troops violated Dinghai, commanding general Zhang Chaofa was defeated and lost the city; Governor Wuer'e and Admiral Zhu Tingbiao forcibly recalled Yunfei from mourning to serve in the army; Governor-General Deng Tingzhen also recommended him as reliable, and he acted as commander of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when British troops attacked Dinghai, commanding general Zhang Chaofa was defeated and lost the city; Governor Wuer'e and Admiral Zhu Tingbiao forcibly recalled Yunfei from mourning to serve; Governor-General Deng Tingzhen also recommended him as reliable, and he was appointed acting commander of Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 雲飛議先守後戰，扼招寶、金雞兩山，列砲江岸，築土城，集失伍舊兵訓練，軍氣始振。

translations.literal: Yunfei proposed holding first and fighting later, holding Zhaobao and Jinji mountains, lining guns along the riverbank, building an earthen wall, gathering scattered old soldiers for training, and army morale was first revived.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfei proposed holding first and fighting later: he held Zhaobao and Jinji mountains, lined guns along the riverbank, built an earthen wall, gathered scattered old soldiers for training, and army morale revived.

sentences.zh: 英人安突得出測量形勢，以計擒之，敵始有戒心。

translations.literal: The Englishman An Tude came out to survey the terrain; Yunfei captured him by stratagem, and the enemy first grew wary.
translations.idiomatic: The Englishman An Tude came out to survey the terrain; Yunfei captured him by stratagem, and the enemy grew wary for the first time.

sentences.zh: 雲飛乘機圖恢復，未果。

translations.literal: Yunfei seized the opportunity to plan recovery, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfei seized the opportunity to plan recovery, but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廣東議款，以香港易定海，欽差大臣伊里布令雲飛率所部渡海收地，然後釋俘，以二鎮帥偕往。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, while Guangdong negotiated a settlement exchanging Hong Kong for Dinghai, Imperial Commissioner Yilibu ordered Yunfei to lead his troops across the sea to recover the territory, then release prisoners, with two commanding generals going together.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, while Guangdong negotiated a settlement exchanging Hong Kong for Dinghai, Imperial Commissioner Yilibu ordered Yunfei to lead his troops across the sea to recover the territory and then release prisoners, with two commanding generals accompanying him.

sentences.zh: 二鎮者，壽春鎮王錫朋、處州鎮鄭國鴻也。

translations.literal: The two commanding generals were Wang Xipeng of Shouchun and Zheng Guohong of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanding generals were Wang Xipeng of Shouchun and Zheng Guohong of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而裕謙代伊里布，改議戰守，雲飛以定海三面皆山，前臨海無蔽，請於道頭築土城，竹山、曉峰嶺增砲台，而道頭南五奎山、吉祥門、毛港悉置防為犄角。

translations.literal: Soon Yu Qian replaced Yilibu and shifted to debating war and defense; Yunfei, because Dinghai was surrounded by mountains on three sides with no cover facing the sea in front, requested building an earthen wall at Daotou, adding batteries at Zhushan and Xiaofeng Ridge, and posting defenses at Wuikui Mountain, Jixiang Gate, and Maogang to the south of Daotou as supporting positions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu Qian replaced Yilibu and shifted to debating war and defense; Yunfei, noting that Dinghai was surrounded by mountains on three sides with no cover facing the sea, requested building an earthen wall at Daotou, adding batteries at Zhushan and Xiaofeng Ridge, and posting defenses at Wuikui Mountain, Jixiang Gate, and Maogang south of Daotou as supporting positions.

sentences.zh: 裕謙以費鉅未盡許，則請借三年廉俸興築，益忤裕謙。

translations.literal: Yu Qian, because the expense was great, did not fully approve; Yunfei then requested borrowing three years of his official salary to build, further offending Yu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, citing the great expense, did not fully approve; Yunfei then offered to borrow against three years of his official salary to fund construction, further offending Yu Qian.

sentences.zh: 尋至定海，見雲飛青布帕首、短衣草履，奔走烈日中；

translations.literal: Soon he arrived at Dinghai and saw Yunfei with a blue cloth wrapped around his head, wearing a short coat and straw sandals, rushing about in the blazing sun;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he arrived at Dinghai and saw Yunfei with a blue cloth wrapped around his head, wearing a short coat and straw sandals, rushing about in the blazing sun;

sentences.zh: 又聞其巡洋捕盜傷臂，奪盜刃刺之，始服其忠勇。

translations.literal: He also heard that while patrolling and capturing pirates Yunfei had injured his arm, seized a pirate's blade and stabbed him with it, and only then came to respect his loyalty and bravery.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that while patrolling and capturing pirates Yunfei had injured his arm, seized a pirate's blade and stabbed him with it, and only then came to respect his loyalty and bravery.

sentences.zh: 迨英兵復來犯，砲擊敵艦於竹山門、東港浦，迭卻之，加提督銜。

translations.literal: When English troops came to attack again, he fired on enemy warships at Zhushan Gate and Donggangpu and repeatedly drove them back; he was granted the rank of admiral.
translations.idiomatic: When British troops attacked again, he fired on enemy warships at Zhushan Gate and Donggangpu and repeatedly drove them back; he was granted the rank of admiral.

sentences.zh: 於是雲飛屯道頭土城，錫朋、國鴻分防曉峰、竹山。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yunfei encamped at the earthen wall at Daotou, while Xipeng and Guohong separately defended Xiaofeng and Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yunfei encamped at the earthen wall at Daotou, while Xipeng and Guohong separately defended Xiaofeng and Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 雲飛獨當敵衝，敵連檣進突，登五奎山，砲擊紅衣夷目，乃退。

translations.literal: Yunfei alone bore the brunt of the enemy assault; the enemy advanced in close succession of ships, scaled Wuikui Mountain, and were driven back after cannon fire struck a red-coated foreign officer.
