translations.idiomatic: Yunfei alone bore the brunt of the enemy assault; the enemy advanced in close succession of ships, scaled Wuikui Mountain, and were driven back after cannon fire struck a red-coated foreign officer.

sentences.zh: 次日，敵蔽山後發砲仰擊，亦隔山應之。

translations.literal: The next day the enemy concealed themselves behind the mountain and fired upward; he also responded from across the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy concealed themselves behind the mountain and fired upward; he responded from across the mountain.

sentences.zh: 夜，敵乘霧至，直逼土城，砲中載藥敵船，轟殲甚眾。

translations.literal: At night the enemy came through the fog, pressed straight to the earthen wall, and cannon fire struck an enemy ship loaded with powder, blasting and killing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: At night the enemy came through the fog and pressed straight to the earthen wall; cannon fire struck an enemy ship loaded with powder, blasting and killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 越日，乃肉搏來奪曉峰嶺，分攻竹山門，錫朋、國鴻皆戰歿，縣城遂陷。

translations.literal: The following day they came in hand-to-hand fighting to seize Xiaofeng Ridge and divided forces to attack Zhushan Gate; Xipeng and Guohong both died in battle, and the county seat then fell.
translations.idiomatic: The following day they came in hand-to-hand fighting to seize Xiaofeng Ridge and divided forces to attack Zhushan Gate; Xipeng and Guohong were both killed in battle, and the county seat fell.

sentences.zh: 敵萃攻土城，雲飛知不可為，出敕印付營弁，率親兵二百，持刀步入敵中，轉鬥二里許，格殺無算。

translations.literal: The enemy massed to attack the earthen wall; Yunfei knew the situation was hopeless, handed out his commission seal to camp officers, led two hundred personal troops, walked with drawn blades into the enemy ranks, and fought for about two li, killing beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy massed against the earthen wall; Yunfei knew the situation was hopeless, handed his commission seal to camp officers, led two hundred personal troops with drawn blades into the enemy ranks, and fought for about two li, killing beyond count.

sentences.zh: 至竹山麓，頭面右手被斫，猶血戰，身受四十餘創，砲洞胸背，植立崖石而死。

translations.literal: At the foot of Zhushan his head, face, and right hand were hacked; he still fought on in bloody combat, received more than forty wounds, was pierced through chest and back by cannon fire, and died standing upright against the cliff rocks.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of Zhushan his head, face, and right hand were hacked; he still fought on, received more than forty wounds, was pierced through chest and back by cannon fire, and died standing upright against the cliff rocks.

sentences.zh: 定海義勇徐保夜負其屍，浮舟渡海。

translations.literal: The Dinghai volunteer Xu Bao carried his corpse on his back by night and crossed the sea in a small boat.
translations.idiomatic: The Dinghai volunteer Xu Bao carried his body on his back by night and crossed the sea in a small boat.

sentences.zh: 是役連戰六晝夜，斃敵千餘，卒以眾寡不敵，三鎮同殉。

translations.literal: In this battle they fought continuously for six days and nights, killed more than a thousand enemy soldiers, but in the end were too few to match the enemy and all three commanding generals died together.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle they fought continuously for six days and nights and killed more than a thousand enemy soldiers, but in the end were too few to match the enemy and all three commanding generals died together.

sentences.zh: 事聞，宣宗揮淚下詔，賜金治喪，卹典依提督例，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡壯節。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, the Xuanzong Emperor wiped away tears and issued an edict, granted gold for funeral expenses, awarded posthumous honors by the standard for admirals, granted a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry together with one of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Emperor Xuanzong wiped away tears and issued an edict, granted gold for funeral expenses, awarded posthumous honors by the standard for admirals, granted hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and posthumously titled him Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 賜兩子文武舉人，以簡襲世職，官至甘肅階州知州；

translations.literal: Both sons were granted the ranks of civil and military licentiate; Jian inherited the hereditary office and rose to prefect of Jiezhou in Gansu;
translations.idiomatic: Both sons were granted the ranks of civil and military licentiate; Jian inherited the hereditary rank and rose to prefect of Jiezhou in Gansu;

sentences.zh: 以敦官守備。

translations.literal: Yidun served as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yidun served as battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 雲飛兼能文，著有名將錄、制械製藥要言、水師緝捕管見、浙海險要圖說及詩文集。

translations.literal: Yunfei was also skilled in letters and authored Records of Famous Generals, Essentials on Making Weapons and Preparing Medicines, Naval Views on Pursuit and Capture, Illustrated Account of Strategic Points on the Zhejiang Seas, and collected poems and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Yunfei was also skilled in letters and authored Records of Famous Generals, Essentials on Making Weapons and Preparing Medicines, Naval Views on Pursuit and Capture, Illustrated Account of Strategic Points on the Zhejiang Seas, and collected poems and prose.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，母亦知大義，喪歸，一慟而止，曰：「吾有子矣！」

translations.literal: He was filial toward his mother; his mother also understood great principle; when the mourning party returned, she wept once and stopped, saying: "I have a son!"
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his mother; his mother also understood the greater cause; when the mourning party returned, she wept once and stopped, saying, "I have a son!"

sentences.zh: 錫朋，字樵傭，順天寧河人。

translations.literal: Xipeng, style name Qiaoyong, a native of Ninghe in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Xipeng, styled Qiaoyong, was a native of Ninghe in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 以武舉授兵部差官，遷固原游擊。

translations.literal: As a military licentiate he was appointed a dispatch officer in the Ministry of War and transferred to battalion commander of Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As a military licentiate he was appointed a dispatch officer in the Ministry of War and transferred to battalion commander of Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 從陝甘總督楊遇春徵回疆，大河拐、洋阿爾巴特、沙布都爾、渾河諸戰並有功，賜花翎，擢湖南臨武營參將。

translations.literal: He followed Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Yang Yuchun in campaigning in the Western Regions and achieved merit at the battles of Daheguai, Yang'a'erbate, Shabuduer, and Hunhe; he was granted the peacock feather and promoted to colonel of the Linwu garrison in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Yang Yuchun in campaigning in the Western Regions and won distinction at the battles of Daheguai, Yang'a'erbate, Shabuduer, and Hunhe; he was granted the peacock feather and promoted to colonel of the Linwu garrison in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從剿江華瑤趙金龍，賜號銳勇巴圖魯，擢寶慶協副將。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he took part in suppressing the Jianghua Yao leader Zhao Jinlong, was granted the title Ruiyong Batulu, and was promoted to vice general of the Baoqing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he took part in suppressing the Jianghua Yao leader Zhao Jinlong, was granted the title Ruiyong Batulu, and was promoted to vice general of the Baoqing garrison.

sentences.zh: 又平廣東連州瑤，功最。

translations.literal: He also pacified the Yao of Lianzhou in Guangdong, achieving the greatest merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also pacified the Yao of Lianzhou in Guangdong, achieving the greatest merit.

sentences.zh: 擢汀州鎮總兵，以憂歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commanding general of Tingzhou and returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commanding general of Tingzhou and returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 十八年，起授壽春鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was recalled and appointed commanding general of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was recalled and appointed commanding general of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 二十年，偕提督陳化成防吳淞，伊里布調援寧波。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he joined Admiral Chen Huacheng in defending Wusong; Yilibu transferred him to reinforce Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he joined Admiral Chen Huacheng in defending Wusong; Yilibu transferred him to reinforce Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 尋偕葛雲飛等守定海。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Ge Yunfei and others in holding Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Ge Yunfei and others in holding Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 敵至，錫朋初守竹山門​​，為諸軍應援，數獲勝。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived, Xipeng first held Zhushan Gate, supporting the other armies, and won several victories.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived, Xipeng first held Zhushan Gate, supporting the other armies, and won several victories.

sentences.zh: 及敵乘霧登曉峰嶺，以無巨砲不能禦，率兵奮擊，並分援竹山，所部裨弁硃匯源、呂林環、劉桂五、夏敏忠、張魁甲先後陣歿，眾且盡，錫朋手刃數人，遂遇害。

translations.literal: When the enemy scaled Xiaofeng Ridge through the fog and could not be repelled for lack of great guns, he led troops in fierce attack and also sent detachments to reinforce Zhushan; his subordinate officers Zhu Huiyuan, Lu Linhuan, Liu Guiwu, Xia Minzhong, and Zhang Kuijia died in battle one after another, his force was nearly exhausted, Xipeng killed several men with his own hand, and then met his death.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy scaled Xiaofeng Ridge through the fog and could not be repelled for lack of great guns, he led troops in a fierce counterattack and also sent detachments to reinforce Zhushan; his subordinate officers Zhu Huiyuan, Lu Linhuan, Liu Guiwu, Xia Minzhong, and Zhang Kuijia were killed in battle one after another, his force was nearly exhausted, Xipeng killed several men with his own hand, and then met his death.

sentences.zh: 久之始得其屍，面如生，耳際有創。

translations.literal: Only after a long time was his corpse recovered; his face was as if alive, with a wound near the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long time was his body recovered; his face looked as if he were still alive, with a wound near the ear.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉韻珂驗實，為改殮，卹典加等，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡剛節。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Yunke verified the facts, had the body re-encoffined, awarded posthumous honors with an added grade, granted a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry together with one of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Gangjie.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Yunke verified the facts, had the body re-encoffined, awarded posthumous honors with an added grade, granted hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry, and posthumously titled him Gangjie.

sentences.zh: 子承泗、承瀚，並賜文舉人，承泗襲世職，官山西溫州知州；

translations.literal: His sons Chengsi and Chenghan were both granted the rank of civil licentiate; Chengsi inherited the hereditary office and served as prefect of Wenzhou in Shanxi;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chengsi and Chenghan were both granted the rank of civil licentiate; Chengsi inherited the hereditary rank and served as prefect of Wenzhou in Shanxi;

sentences.zh: 承瀚工部主事。

translations.literal: Chenghan served as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghan served as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 國鴻，字雪堂，湖南鳳凰廳人。

translations.literal: Guohong, style name Xuetang, a native of Fenghuang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Guohong, styled Xuetang, was a native of Fenghuang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父朝桂，貴州副將。

translations.literal: His father Chaogui was vice general of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chaogui was vice general of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 伯父廷松，鎮筸千總，殉苗難，無子，以國鴻嗣，襲雲騎尉。

translations.literal: His uncle Tingsong, a company commander of Zhenqian, died in martyrdom during the Miao troubles and had no son; Guohong was made his heir and inherited the office of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Tingsong, a company commander of Zhenqian, died during the Miao troubles and had no son; Guohong was made his heir and inherited the rank of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從傅鼐剿苗，授永綏屯守備，洊擢寶慶副將。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Nai in suppressing the Miao, was appointed battalion commander of the Yongshui garrison, and was repeatedly promoted to vice general of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Nai in suppressing the Miao, was appointed battalion commander of the Yongshui garrison, and was promoted repeatedly to vice general of Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年，擢處州鎮總兵，調防鎮海，充翼長。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang he was promoted to commanding general of Chuzhou, transferred to defend Zhenhai, and served as wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Daoguang he was promoted to commanding general of Chuzhou, transferred to defend Zhenhai, and served as wing commander.

sentences.zh: 定海既還，移兵分守要隘。

translations.literal: Once Dinghai was recovered, he moved troops to hold strategic passes in separate detachments.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dinghai was recovered, he moved troops to hold strategic passes in separate detachments.

sentences.zh: 敵艦初犯竹山門，國鴻發巨砲斷其桅，遂以竹山為分汛地。

translations.literal: When enemy warships first violated Zhushan Gate, Guohong fired great guns and broke their masts, and thereafter made Zhushan his separate garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy warships first attacked Zhushan Gate, Guohong fired great guns and broke their masts, and thereafter made Zhushan his separate garrison post.

sentences.zh: 戰連日，久雨，往來泥淖。

translations.literal: Fighting continued for days; prolonged rain made travel through mud and mire.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued for days in prolonged rain, with men trudging through mud and mire.

sentences.zh: 及敵分三路同時來撲，國鴻奮擊，槍砲皆熱不可用，短兵拒戰，而土寇導敵奪曉峰嶺，險要盡失，國鴻單騎衝陣，被數十創而殞，依總兵賜卹，予騎都尉世職，追諡忠節。

translations.literal: When the enemy divided into three columns and attacked simultaneously, Guohong fought fiercely; guns and cannon grew too hot to use and he fought at close quarters; local bandits guided the enemy to seize Xiaofeng Ridge and all strategic points were lost; Guohong charged the enemy lines alone on horseback, received several dozen wounds and died; posthumous honors were granted by the standard for commanding generals, a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded, and he was posthumously titled Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy divided into three columns and attacked simultaneously, Guohong fought fiercely; guns and cannon grew too hot to use and he fought at close quarters; local bandits guided the enemy to seize Xiaofeng Ridge and all strategic points were lost; Guohong charged the enemy lines alone on horseback, received dozens of wounds and fell; posthumous honors were granted by the standard for commanding generals, a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded, and he was posthumously titled Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 子鼎聲已歿，賜其孫鍔、銛並為舉人，鍔襲騎都尉，七品小京官；

translations.literal: His son Dingsheng had already died; his grandsons E and Xian were both granted the rank of licentiate; E inherited the Commandant of Cavalry and served as a seventh-rank junior capital official;
translations.idiomatic: His son Dingsheng had already died; his grandsons E and Xian were both granted the rank of licentiate; E inherited the rank of Commandant of Cavalry and served as a seventh-rank junior capital official;

sentences.zh: 銛襲雲騎尉。

translations.literal: Xian inherited the Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xian inherited the rank of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出繼之子鼎臣，批驗大使，從軍中，揚威將軍奕經令募水勇攻敵海山港，賜花翎、四品頂戴。

translations.literal: His adopted son Dingchen, an inspection envoy, followed the army; General Yijing ordered him to recruit naval braves to attack the enemy at Haishan Harbor and granted him the peacock feather and a fourth-rank official's button.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Dingchen, an inspection envoy, followed the army; General Yijing ordered him to recruit naval braves to attack the enemy at Haishan Harbor and granted him the peacock feather and a fourth-rank official's button.

sentences.zh: 三鎮死事最烈，併入昭忠祠。

translations.literal: The three commanding generals died most heroically and were all enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanding generals died most heroically and were all enshrined in the Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 定海收復，建立專祠，合祀雲飛、錫朋，並許原籍各建專祠。

translations.literal: When Dinghai was recovered, a dedicated shrine was built jointly enshrining Yunfei and Xipeng, and permission was granted to build dedicated shrines in their native districts as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Dinghai was recovered, a dedicated shrine was built jointly enshrining Yunfei and Xipeng, and permission was granted to build dedicated shrines in their native districts as well.

sentences.zh: 當定海之初陷也，總兵張朝發戰於港口，兵敗，身受砲傷，知縣姚懷祥、典史全福皆死之。

translations.literal: When Dinghai first fell, commanding general Zhang Chaofa fought at the harbor, was defeated, was himself wounded by cannon fire, and Prefect Yao Huaixiang and archivist Quan Fu both died.
translations.idiomatic: When Dinghai first fell, commanding general Zhang Chaofa fought at the harbor, was defeated and wounded by cannon fire, and Prefect Yao Huaixiang and archivist Quan Fu both died.

sentences.zh: 時咎朝發不專守陸路，巡撫烏爾恭額疏劾逮治。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Chaofa was blamed for not concentrating on holding the land route; Governor Wuer'e memorialized to impeach and have him arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Chaofa was blamed for not concentrating on holding the land route; Governor Wuer'e memorialized to impeach and have him arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 朝發已以傷殞，卹典不及焉。

translations.literal: Chaofa had already died of his wounds, and posthumous honors did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofa had already died of his wounds, and posthumous honors were not granted.

sentences.zh: 浙中戰事以定海為最力。

translations.literal: Among the battles in Zhejiang, those at Dinghai were fought with the greatest effort.
translations.idiomatic: Among the battles in Zhejiang, those at Dinghai were fought with the greatest effort.

sentences.zh: 後揚威將軍奕經督師，將帥多闒茸，戰事如兒戲，惟金華協副將硃貴稱忠勇。

translations.literal: Later, when General Yijing directed the army, most commanders were incompetent and the fighting was like child's play; only Zhu Gui, vice general of the Jinhua garrison, was praised for loyalty and bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when General Yijing directed the army, most commanders were incompetent and the fighting was treated like child's play; only Zhu Gui, vice general of the Jinhua garrison, was praised for loyalty and bravery.

sentences.zh: 貴，字黻堂，甘肅河州人。

translations.literal: Gui, style name Futang, a native of Hezhou in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui, styled Futang, was a native of Hezhou in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 以武生入伍，從征川、陝教匪，剿藍號賊於盧家灣。

translations.literal: As a military student he entered the ranks, campaigned against the sect rebels in Sichuan and Shaanxi, and suppressed Blue Banner rebels at Lujiawan.
translations.idiomatic: As a military student he entered the ranks, campaigned against the sect rebels in Sichuan and Shaanxi, and suppressed Blue Banner rebels at Lujiawan.

sentences.zh: 賊渠冉學勝伏密箐中，以長矛刺傷主將，貴奪其矛而擒之，勇冠軍中。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Ran Xuesheng lay hidden in a dense ravine and stabbed the commanding general with a long spear; Gui seized the spear and captured him, his bravery foremost in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Ran Xuesheng lay hidden in a dense ravine and stabbed the commanding general with a long spear; Gui seized the spear and captured him, his bravery foremost in the army.

sentences.zh: 滑縣、三才峽諸役，皆在事有功，累擢涼州守備。

translations.literal: At the campaigns of Huaxian, Sancaixia, and elsewhere he achieved merit on all occasions and was repeatedly promoted to battalion commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the campaigns of Huaxian, Sancaixia, and elsewhere he won distinction on all occasions and was promoted repeatedly to battalion commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道光初，從楊遇春戰回疆，擢游擊，歷陝西西安參將、署察漢托洛亥副將。

translations.literal: In the early Daoguang reign he followed Yang Yuchun in fighting in the Western Regions, was promoted to battalion commander, and served successively as colonel of Xi'an in Shaanxi and acting vice general of Chahantuoluohei.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Daoguang reign he followed Yang Yuchun in fighting in the Western Regions, was promoted to battalion commander, and served successively as colonel of Xi'an in Shaanxi and acting vice general of Chahantuoluohei.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢浙江金華協副將。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to vice general of the Jinhua garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to vice general of the Jinhua garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 揚威將軍奕經督師，貴率陝甘兵九百以從。

translations.literal: When General Yijing directed the army, Gui led nine hundred Shaanxi-Gansu troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When General Yijing directed the army, Gui led nine hundred Shaanxi-Gansu troops to follow him.

sentences.zh: 時兵多新募，惟貴所部最號勁旅。

translations.literal: At the time most troops were newly recruited; only Gui's command was called the strongest force.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most troops were newly recruited; only Gui's command was considered the strongest force.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，奕經規复寧波、鎮海，令貴當鎮海一路，行未至，寧波已失利，止勿進，調赴長谿嶺大營，遂屯慈谿城西大寶山。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year Yijing planned to recover Ningbo and Zhenhai and ordered Gui to take the Zhenhai route; before he arrived Ningbo had already suffered defeat, he was ordered not to advance, was transferred to the main camp at Changxiling, and then encamped at Dabaoshan west of Cixi city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-second year Yijing planned to recover Ningbo and Zhenhai and ordered Gui to take the Zhenhai route; before he arrived Ningbo had already suffered defeat, he was ordered not to advance, was transferred to the main camp at Changxiling, and encamped at Dabaoshan west of Cixi city.

sentences.zh: 敵乘勝以二千人自大西壩登岸，貴率所部迎擊，斃敵四百餘人。

translations.literal: The enemy, riding their victory, landed two thousand men from Daxiba; Gui led his troops to meet them and killed more than four hundred enemy soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, riding their victory, landed two thousand men from Daxiba; Gui led his troops to meet them and killed more than four hundred enemy soldiers.

sentences.zh: 再卻再進，自辰至申，軍中不得食，猶酣戰。

translations.literal: They were driven back and advanced again; from the chen hour to the shen hour the army had nothing to eat yet still fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: They were driven back and advanced again; from morning to afternoon the army had nothing to eat yet still fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 鄉勇忽亂隊，敵由山後鈔襲，增者幾倍。

translations.literal: The local braves suddenly fell into disorder; the enemy flanked from behind the mountain and their numbers increased several times over.
translations.idiomatic: The local braves suddenly fell into disorder; the enemy flanked from behind the mountain and their numbers swelled several times over.

sentences.zh: 又三艦自丈亭江直逼山下，長谿大營驚潰。

translations.literal: Three more warships came straight down from Zhangting River toward the foot of the mountain, and the main camp at Changxi collapsed in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Three more warships came straight down from Zhangting River toward the foot of the mountain, and the main camp at Changxi collapsed in panic.

sentences.zh: 貴腹背被攻，怒馬斫陣，中槍馬倒，躍起奪敵矛奮鬥，傷要害，乃踣。

translations.literal: Gui was attacked from front and rear; he charged the enemy lines on a furious horse, was struck by gunfire and his horse fell; he leaped up, seized an enemy spear and fought on, was wounded in a vital spot, and then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was attacked from front and rear; he charged the enemy lines on a furious horse, was struck by gunfire and his horse fell; he leaped up, seized an enemy spear and fought on, was wounded in a vital spot, and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 子武生昭南，以身障父，同時陣亡。

translations.literal: His son Zhaonan, a military student, shielded his father with his body and died on the battlefield at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaonan, a military student, shielded his father with his body and was killed on the battlefield at the same time.

sentences.zh: 部下游擊黃泰，守備徐宦、陳芝蘭，浙江候補知縣顏履敬等，兵卒三百餘人，同死。

translations.literal: His subordinates battalion commander Huang Tai, battalion commanders Xu Huan and Chen Zhilan, acting prefect of Zhejiang Yan Lujing, and more than three hundred soldiers died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates battalion commander Huang Tai, battalion commanders Xu Huan and Chen Zhilan, acting prefect of Zhejiang Yan Lujing, and more than three hundred soldiers died alongside him.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其忠勇，依總兵例賜卹，予騎都尉世職，子廷瑞襲。

translations.literal: An edict commended his loyalty and bravery; posthumous honors were granted by the standard for commanding generals; a hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded, which son Tingrui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his loyalty and bravery; posthumous honors were granted by the standard for commanding generals; a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry was awarded, which son Tingrui inherited.

sentences.zh: 昭南予雲騎尉世職，子輶甫四歲，命及歲襲職。

translations.literal: Zhaonan was granted a hereditary office of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry; his son You was only four years old and was ordered to inherit the office when he came of age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaonan was granted a hereditary rank of Minor Commandant of Cloud Cavalry; his son You was only four years old and was ordered to inherit the rank when he came of age.

sentences.zh: 阿木穰，世襲土司，大金河千總，加副將銜、巴圖魯勇號。

translations.literal: Amurang, hereditary native official, company commander of the Dajin River, granted the rank of vice general and the brave title Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Amurang, a hereditary native official and company commander of the Dajin River, was granted the rank of vice general and the brave title Batulu.

sentences.zh: 哈克里，瓦寺土守備，率金川屯練赴軍，皆趫捷奮勇，戰輒爭先。

translations.literal: Hakeli, native battalion commander of Wasi, led Jinchuan garrison militia to the army; all were agile and fierce, always vying to be first in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hakeli, native battalion commander of Wasi, led Jinchuan garrison militia to the army; all were agile and fierce, always vying to be first in battle.

sentences.zh: 冠虎形，奕經佔有虎頭之兆，令赴前敵，從提督段永福攻寧波。

translations.literal: They wore tiger shapes on their heads; Yijing had divined an omen of a tiger's head and ordered them to the front, following Admiral Duan Yongfu in attacking Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: They wore tiger shapes on their heads; Yijing had divined an omen of a tiger's head and ordered them to the front, following Admiral Duan Yongfu in attacking Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 敵已為備，至則城門不閉。

translations.literal: The enemy had already made preparations; when they arrived the city gates were not closed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already made preparations; when they arrived the city gates were not closed.

sentences.zh: 阿木穰率土司兵先入，中地雷同歿。

translations.literal: Amurang led the native troops in first and was killed by a land mine.
translations.idiomatic: Amurang led the native troops in first and was killed by a land mine.

sentences.zh: 哈克里攻奪招寶山，猱升而上，搶入威遠城。

translations.literal: Hakeli attacked and seized Zhaobaoshan, climbing like monkeys upward and rushing into Weiyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: Hakeli attacked and seized Zhaobaoshan, climbing like monkeys and rushing into Weiyuan City.

sentences.zh: 敵艦自金雞山翦江至，用砲仰擊，遂不支而退，後亦殉難，浙人哀之。

translations.literal: Enemy warships came slicing down the river from Jinji Mountain and fired upward with cannon; they could not hold and withdrew, and later also died in martyrdom; the people of Zhejiang mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy warships came slicing down the river from Jinji Mountain and fired upward with cannon; they could not hold and withdrew, and later also died; the people of Zhejiang mourned them.

sentences.zh: 自硃貴大寶山之戰，敵受創甚鉅，遂戒深入，慈谿縣城獲完。

translations.literal: After Zhu Gui's battle at Dabaoshan the enemy suffered very heavy losses and then refrained from advancing deeply; Cixi county seat was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Gui's battle at Dabaoshan the enemy suffered very heavy losses and then refrained from advancing deeply; Cixi county seat was preserved intact.

sentences.zh: 士民思其功，為建祠報賽，阿木穰、哈克里亦附祀焉。

translations.literal: Officials and people remembered his achievement and built a shrine to repay his merit; Amurang and Hakeli were also enshrined there.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people remembered his achievement and built a shrine in his honor; Amurang and Hakeli were also enshrined there.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：海疆戰事起，既絀於兵械，又昧於敵情，又牽掣於和戰之無定，畏葸者敗，忠勇者亦敗。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the coastal war began, they were first inferior in arms, then ignorant of the enemy's situation, then constrained by the uncertainty of war and peace; the timid were defeated, and the loyal and brave were defeated as well.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: When the coastal war began, they were first outmatched in arms, then ignorant of the enemy's situation, then constrained by the uncertainty of war and peace; the timid were defeated, and the loyal and brave were defeated as well.

sentences.zh: 專閫之臣，忘身殉國，義不返踵，亦各求其心之所安耳。

translations.literal: Regional commanders who forgot themselves and died for the state, who in righteousness would not turn back, each sought only what would set his heart at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders who forgot themselves and died for the state, who in righteousness would not turn back, each sought only what would set his heart at ease.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，烈已！

translations.literal: Alas, how heroic!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how heroic they were!

sentences.zh: 偏裨授命者，附著於篇。

translations.literal: Subordinate officers who gave their lives are appended in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officers who gave their lives are recorded in this chapter.
